tools.name: list-gpu-types
tools.description: List available GPU types with stock/pricing and capability filters (minimum VRAM, secure/community cloud, name search). Use this to discover valid gpuTypeIds before creating a pod or endpoint. On v2 the realtime stock filter is a no-op.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

minMemoryGb.description: Filter to GPUs with at least this much VRAM in GB

secureCloudOnly.description: Filter to only GPUs available in secure cloud

communityCloudOnly.description: Filter to only GPUs available in community cloud

searchTerm.description: Search term to filter GPUs by name (e.g., 'A100', 'RTX 4090')

includeUnavailable.description: Include GPUs that are currently out of stock. Default is false

tools.name: list-data-centers
tools.description: List Runpod data centers (id, name, region/location). Use this to discover valid dataCenterIds for placing pods, endpoints, or network volumes.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

tools.name: list-cpu-types
tools.description: List available CPU flavor types for CPU pods/endpoints. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

tools.name: get-gpu-type
tools.description: Get details for a single GPU type by id. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API (use list-gpu-types there).

gpuTypeId.description: ID of the GPU type to retrieve

tools.name: get-cpu-type
tools.description: Get details for a single CPU flavor type by id. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API (use list-cpu-types there).

cpuTypeId.description: ID of the CPU type to retrieve

tools.name: get-data-center
tools.description: Get details for a single data center by id. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API (use list-data-centers there).

dataCenterId.description: ID of the data center to retrieve

tools.name: list-pods
tools.description: List your pods (running and stopped) with optional filters — compute type, GPU type, data center, name — plus machine/network-volume expansion. Paginated via limit/cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

computeType.description: Filter to only GPU or only CPU Pods

gpuTypeId.description: Filter to Pods with any of the listed GPU types

dataCenterId.description: Filter to Pods in any of the provided data centers

name.description: Filter to Pods with the provided name

includeNetworkVolume.description: Include information about attached network volumes

tools.name: get-pod
tools.description: Get full details for one pod by id, optionally expanding machine and attached network-volume info.

podId.description: ID of the pod to retrieve

includeNetworkVolume.description: Include information about attached network volumes

tools.name: create-pod
tools.description: Create a new GPU/CPU pod on Runpod. Pass gpuTypeIds for a GPU pod, or computeType:"CPU" for a CPU pod (CPU pods are served by the v1 API for now). If the user does not specify an image, recommend the "Runpod Pytorch 2.8.0" image (runpod/pytorch:1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404) as the default — it has the most up-to-date CUDA and PyTorch versions.

computeType.description: Pod type. On v2, required when not passing gpuTypeIds. 'CPU' is served by the v1 API for now (v2 has no CPU pods yet).

tools.name: update-pod
tools.description: Update a pod's mutable fields (name, image, container disk, volume, ports, env). Only the fields you provide change.

podId.description: ID of the pod to update

containerDiskInGb.description: New container disk size in GB

volumeMountPath.description: New path to mount the volume

tools.name: start-pod
tools.description: Start a stopped pod (resumes the same pod and its billing).

podId.description: ID of the pod to start

tools.name: stop-pod
tools.description: Stop a running pod. The pod and its disk persist; GPU billing stops.

podId.description: ID of the pod to stop

tools.name: restart-pod
tools.description: Restart a running pod (single PodAction call). v2-only — on the v1 API returns a 501 notice (stop then start the pod instead).

podId.description: ID of the pod to restart

tools.name: delete-pod
tools.description: Permanently delete a pod and its data. This cannot be undone.

podId.description: ID of the pod to delete

tools.name: list-endpoints
tools.description: List your Serverless endpoints, optionally expanding template and worker details (v1 only). Paginated via limit/cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

tools.name: get-endpoint
tools.description: Get one Serverless endpoint by id, optionally expanding template and worker details (v1 only).

endpointId.description: ID of the endpoint to retrieve

tools.name: create-endpoint
tools.description: Create a Serverless endpoint. On v2 (default), pass an inline config: imageName + gpuPoolIds (GPU pool names from list-gpu-types — the `pool` field, e.g. AMPERE_80/ADA_24) plus optional workers/scaling/disk/env. On v1, pass a templateId instead. Worker min/max set autoscaling bounds (min 0 = scale to zero).

imageName.description: Docker image (v2). Required on v2 instead of a templateId.

gpuPoolIds.description: GPU pool names (v2, required). The `pool` field from list-gpu-types, e.g. ["AMPERE_80"]. NOT GPU type ids.

containerRegistryAuthId.description: Container registry auth id for a private image (v2)

idleTimeout.description: Idle timeout in seconds before scaling a worker down

tools.name: update-endpoint
tools.description: Update a Serverless endpoint's config. On v2 you can change image/disk/env/ports/registry/workers/scaling/networkVolumes/timeout/flashboot; on v1, scaling fields (worker min/max, idle timeout, scaler type/value, name). Only provided fields change.

endpointId.description: ID of the endpoint to update

containerDiskInGb.description: New container disk size in GB (v2)

executionTimeoutMs.description: New per-job execution timeout in ms (v2)

tools.name: delete-endpoint
tools.description: Permanently delete a Serverless endpoint. This cannot be undone.

endpointId.description: ID of the endpoint to delete

tools.name: list-endpoint-workers
tools.description: List the workers backing a Serverless endpoint, with their status and an aggregate summary. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API. Paginated via limit/cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint whose workers to list

tools.name: run-endpoint
tools.description: Submit an asynchronous job to a Serverless endpoint. Returns a job ID immediately — use get-job-status to poll for results. Async results are available for 30 minutes after completion.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint to run

input.description: Input payload for the worker handler. The expected fields depend on the deployed model or worker.

webhook.description: Webhook URL to receive job completion notifications instead of polling

ttl.description: Time-to-live for the job result in milliseconds

s3Config.description: S3-compatible storage config for large outputs

tools.name: runsync-endpoint
tools.description: Submit a synchronous job to a Serverless endpoint and wait for the result. Best for tasks completing within 90 seconds. If processing exceeds 90 seconds, the response returns a job ID to poll with get-job-status. Max payload: 20 MB. Results expire after 1 minute. Use the wait parameter to extend the server-side wait up to 5 minutes (300000 ms).

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint to run synchronously

input.description: Input payload for the worker handler. The expected fields depend on the deployed model or worker.

wait.description: How long in milliseconds the server should wait for a result before returning a job ID to poll (1000–300000). Defaults to 90000 (90 seconds).

webhook.description: Webhook URL to receive job completion notifications instead of polling

ttl.description: Time-to-live for the job result in milliseconds

s3Config.description: S3-compatible storage config for large outputs

tools.name: get-job-status
tools.description: Check the status of an asynchronous Serverless job. Returns the current status and output when complete. Job statuses: IN_QUEUE, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint the job belongs to

jobId.description: ID of the job to check

tools.name: stream-job
tools.description: Retrieve all streaming output from a Serverless job by polling until the job reaches a terminal state. The worker must support streaming output. Polls /stream/{jobId} repeatedly and collects every chunk until status is COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED, or TIMED_OUT.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint the job belongs to

jobId.description: ID of the job to stream results from

tools.name: cancel-job
tools.description: Cancel a Serverless job that is queued or in progress.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint the job belongs to

jobId.description: ID of the job to cancel

tools.name: retry-job
tools.description: Retry a failed or timed-out Serverless job. Only works for jobs with FAILED or TIMED_OUT status. The previous output is removed and the job is requeued.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint the job belongs to

jobId.description: ID of the job to retry

tools.name: endpoint-health
tools.description: Get the health and operational status of a Serverless endpoint, including worker counts and job statistics.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint to check health for

tools.name: purge-endpoint-queue
tools.description: Remove all pending jobs from a Serverless endpoint queue. Only affects queued jobs — in-progress jobs continue running. Use this for error recovery or clearing outdated requests.

endpointId.description: ID of the Serverless endpoint to purge the queue for

tools.name: list-templates
tools.description: List available templates. By default returns only the user's own templates. Use includeRunpodTemplates to also include official Runpod templates. The recommended default template for new pods is "Runpod Pytorch 2.8.0" (ID: runpod-torch-v280) — it has the latest CUDA and PyTorch versions.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

includeRunpodTemplates.description: Include official Runpod templates in the response

includePublicTemplates.description: Include community-made public templates in the response

includeEndpointBoundTemplates.description: Include templates bound to Serverless endpoints in the response

tools.name: get-template
tools.description: Get one template by id (image, env, ports, disk/volume config).

templateId.description: ID of the template to retrieve

tools.name: create-template
tools.description: Create a reusable pod/endpoint template (image, ports, env, disk/volume). On v2 a category is required and defaults to NVIDIA.

category.description: Hardware category for the template. On v2 a category is required and defaults to NVIDIA when omitted — set CPU or AMD for non-NVIDIA templates so they are not mis-categorized.

containerRegistryAuthId.description: ID of a container registry credential (from create-container-registry-auth / list-container-registry-auths) used to pull a private image. Required when imageName points at a private registry; without it serverless workers fail the image pull.

tools.name: update-template
tools.description: Update a template's mutable fields (name, image, ports, env, readme). Only provided fields change.

templateId.description: ID of the template to update

readme.description: New README content in markdown format

containerRegistryAuthId.description: ID of a container registry credential (from create-container-registry-auth / list-container-registry-auths) used to pull a private image. Set this to attach a credential to a template referencing a private registry.

tools.name: delete-template
tools.description: Permanently delete a template. This cannot be undone.

templateId.description: ID of the template to delete

tools.name: list-network-volumes
tools.description: List your network volumes (persistent storage attachable to pods). Paginated via limit/cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

tools.name: get-network-volume
tools.description: Get one network volume by id (name, size, data center).

networkVolumeId.description: ID of the network volume to retrieve

tools.name: create-network-volume
tools.description: Create a persistent network volume in a data center (size 1–4000 GB) that pods can mount.

tools.name: update-network-volume
tools.description: Update a network volume (rename, or grow size — the new size must exceed the current size). Only provided fields change.

networkVolumeId.description: ID of the network volume to update

name.description: New name for the network volume

size.description: New size in GB (must be larger than current)

tools.name: delete-network-volume
tools.description: Permanently delete a network volume and its data. This cannot be undone.

networkVolumeId.description: ID of the network volume to delete

tools.name: list-container-registry-auths
tools.description: List your saved container-registry credentials (private image-pull auth). Paginated via limit/cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

tools.name: get-container-registry-auth
tools.description: Get one saved container-registry credential by id (the secret/password is not returned).

containerRegistryAuthId.description: ID of the container registry auth to retrieve

tools.name: create-container-registry-auth
tools.description: Save container-registry credentials (username + password/token) so pods and endpoints can pull private images.

name.description: Name for the container registry auth

password.description: Registry password or access token (stored as a secret)

tools.name: delete-container-registry-auth
tools.description: Permanently delete a saved container-registry credential. This cannot be undone.

containerRegistryAuthId.description: ID of the container registry auth to delete

tools.name: list-tags
tools.description: List your tags (key/value labels on pods, volumes, clusters, and endpoints). v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API. Paginated via limit/cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

includeResources.description: Include the resources attached to each tag in the response

tools.name: get-tag
tools.description: Get one tag by id, optionally including its attached resources. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

tagId.description: ID of the tag to retrieve

includeResources.description: Include the resources attached to this tag

tools.name: create-tag
tools.description: Create a key/value tag, optionally attaching resources at creation. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

id.description: Resource identifier (e.g. a pod or endpoint id)

type.description: Type of resource to associate with the tag

resources.description: Resources to attach to the tag at creation time

tools.name: update-tag
tools.description: Update a tag (rename its key/value, or replace its resource associations). Provide at least one of key, value, or resources. Sending resources:[] removes all associations; omitting resources leaves them unchanged. Replacing resources is NOT atomic — a failed update can leave a partially-applied set, so for small association changes prefer attach-tag/detach-tag. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

tagId.description: ID of the tag to update

id.description: Resource identifier (e.g. a pod or endpoint id)

type.description: Type of resource to associate with the tag

resources.description: Replace the tag's resource associations with exactly these. Omit to leave unchanged; pass [] to detach all.

tools.name: delete-tag
tools.description: Permanently delete a tag (removes it from all resources it is attached to). This cannot be undone. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

tagId.description: ID of the tag to delete

tools.name: attach-tag
tools.description: Attach a tag to a resource (pod, network volume, cluster, or serverless endpoint). Idempotent — attaching an already-associated resource is a no-op. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

resourceType.description: Type of resource to attach the tag to

resourceId.description: ID of the resource to attach the tag to

tools.name: detach-tag
tools.description: Detach a tag from a resource (removes the association only — the resource and tag are not deleted). Idempotent — detaching a resource that is not associated is a no-op. v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API.

resourceType.description: Type of resource to detach the tag from

resourceId.description: ID of the resource to detach the tag from

tools.name: get-billing
tools.description: Get time-bucketed Runpod spend history, either aggregated across all resources or broken down by resource type (pods, serverless, endpoints, network volumes, clusters). v2-only — returns a 501 notice on the v1 API. Records are capped via limit/cursor; narrow the window with startTime/endTime or lastN.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20, max 100). Use the returned nextCursor to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response (nextCursor). Omit to start from the beginning.

scope.description: Which billing breakdown to fetch. "all" (default) is the aggregate across every resource.

startTime.description: Start of the period (RFC 3339, e.g. 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z). Defaults to 30 days ago. Mutually exclusive with lastN.

endTime.description: End of the period (RFC 3339), exclusive. Defaults to now. Mutually exclusive with lastN.

bucketSize.description: Length of each time bucket. Defaults to day.

lastN.description: Return the last N buckets of bucketSize, ending with the current one. Mutually exclusive with startTime/endTime.
